actions.action: Check whether the soil is dense, soggy, or staying wet
Smell the base of the plant for a sour or rotting odor
Slide the plant out of its pot and inspect the roots
If roots are rotting, rinse off the soil and cut away mushy roots with sterilized shears
Clean the pot with soap and water
Repot in fresh, well-draining mix amended with perlite or bark, in a pot with drainage holes
Prune back some top foliage to balance the reduced roots
Move the plant indoors to a spot with bright, indirect light
Check whether it needs potting on to a bigger pot
Water only once the soil is bone dry

verdict.reason: The answer blames wet soil but leads with root rot rather than transplant shock and low light, and its bright-light advice is buried behind root surgery that only applies if rot is found, so it is not clearly harmful.
